textbookText: The minus sign that appears in the equation needs an explanation. It means that the direction of the vector electric field is always opposite to the variation of the potential (∆𝑉 ) of a positive charge. So, travel in the opposite direction to that of the feld means moving to a position of higher potential and thus a positive gain in potential. In figure (a) the motion of the positive charge is to the left, ∆𝑉 is negative (final state minus initial state: 0 V - 12 V); so, according to Physics, Grade 11 | 409

the equation, E will be positive and this tells us that the motion is in the direction of the field. In other words, going upstream in the field (against the field) means going to higher potential so a gain in potential (positive change in ∆𝑉). Going downstream, ∆𝑉 is negative and E is positive (product of two minus signs) indicating the motion is in the direction of field. If an electron moves from 0 V towards the 12 V plate (a position of higher potential) its potential energy is reduced because the potential energy change ∆𝐸𝑝 is given by 𝑒∆𝑉 as usual, but here 𝑒 is negative and ∆𝑉 is positive. The electron will accelerate in this direction if free to do so gaining kinetic energy from the field at the expense of the electrical potential energy. 21.7 Similarities between Electric and Gravitation Fields
A comparison between Newton’s law of gravitation and Coulomb’s law shows that there are many similarities between the actions of the two types of force. There are also some important differences.
The main similarities are as follows:
i) Both electric and gravitational forces are non-contact; forces are exerted over a distance without direct contact. ii) Both forces are of infinite range. iii) Both forces obey inverse square laws.
The main differences are as follows:

i) Gravitational forces between masses are always attractive; electric forces can be attractive or repulsive. ii) An electric force is much stronger than the gravitational force. iii) It is possible to shield an electric force, but the gravitational force acts on all objects. iv) An electric force only acts on charged objects; the gravitational force acts on all objects.
